ProviderSettings._comment_Ollama_LineEdit: RepeatPenalty 1.3 breaks the LineEdit repetition loop observed live (Dicta fell into a 335s loop emitting ~10 identical suggestions + 'לא,'->'לא' punctuation noise before the JSON truncated mid-object). The loop is a decoding failure, so a repeat penalty ABOVE the 1.1 ProviderTuningOptions default and the 1.2 LinguisticAnalysis value is the primary fix; the post-parse dedupe/no-op/cap in UnifiedAnalysisService.NormalizeLineEditSuggestions is the structural backstop. Keep NumPredict 5120 and Temperature 0.2 as-is.
ProviderSettings._comment_Ollama_BookReview: Whole-book developmental review (wb2). Each per-dimension call sends the ENTIRE budgeted book context ([BOOK_CONTEXT] = BookBrief + many ChapterBriefs) and the model emits a per-chapter dimensionSignals scratch block BEFORE the findings, so BOTH input and output scale with chapter count. WITHOUT this entry AiTaskType.BookReview falls back to NumCtx=4096 (the implicit ProviderTuningOptions default, NOT the Ollama entry's 8192) — on a 15+ chapter book the input alone overflows 4096, Ollama TRUNCATES the prompt, and the model returns a lone '{' so ExtractJson fails and EVERY dimension returns null (job falsely Succeeded with 0 findings). NumCtx=16384 fits a large book's input+output (book budget derives as NumCtx*0.5≈8192 tokens, matching LinguisticAnalysis); NumPredict=6144 gives the dimensionSignals+findings output room to complete on a 20-40 chapter book. Verified live (gemma4:12b, 16-chapter synthetic): default 4096 -> 1-char '{' (6/6 fail); 16384/6144 -> complete valid JSON, findings parse. KEEP IN SYNC with the cloud counterpart entries below (p1-5, model-tier-fast-thinking plan): OpenRouter_BookReview / OpenAI_BookReview / Azure_BookReview / Anthropic_BookReview (see _comment_OpenRouterPerTask and _comment_CloudBookReviewFloor) mirror this same NumCtx=16384 window on purpose, and BookReview is the one task that MUST have an explicit window on every registered provider without exception — routing BookReview at a provider whose entry omits NumCtx reproduces exactly this comment's failure mode via the OTHER provider, silently. If this entry's NumCtx or NumPredict ever changes, re-check whether the cloud entries should move too (they need not match in VALUE, since NumCtx is never sent to a cloud provider and only sizes the local input budget, but the failure this comment documents is universal across providers).
ProviderSettings._comment_Ollama_AnalysisRepair: Value-scoped analysis-output repair (analysis-output-repair plan, p3). AnalysisRepairService sends ONE analysis prose field at a time to gemma4:12b for a Hebrew cleanup (remove leaked English terms/garbles) with structure held by code, so 16384 ctx is ample headroom for a single field + the verbatim repair instruction and NumPredict 2048 fits a repaired field. Low Temperature (0.2) keeps the repair conservative. KEEP IN SYNC with FeatureModels:AnalysisRepair below (both must exist for the repair pass to route to gemma4:12b); the Ai:AnalysisRepair block (Enabled/GuardOnly/PerType) gates whether the pass RUNS, these keys only ROUTE.
ProviderSettings._comment_Ollama_TermRepair: Span-scoped DYNAMIC term repair (dynamic-term-repair-design plan, d3/d4). DynamicTermRepairService sends ONE «marked» foreign run at a time and asks for a tiny {"replacement":"..."} JSON token, so the output is minute (NumPredict 256 is generous headroom) while 16384 ctx comfortably fits the whole marked value + the verbatim repair instruction (mirrors Ollama_AnalysisRepair's ctx for the same reason). Low Temperature (0.2) keeps the repair conservative, matching AnalysisRepair/TermRepair's shared 'never invent, only substitute' contract. KEEP IN SYNC with FeatureModels:TermRepair below; the Ai:AnalysisRepair.Mode knob (Off/Glossary/Dynamic/GlossaryThenDynamic) gates whether this pass RUNS AT ALL (shipped default Mode=GlossaryThenDynamic now calls it after the glossary; Mode=Glossary/Off is the rollback that skips it), these keys only ROUTE.
ProviderSettings._comment_Ollama_GenericChat: CALLER SET, re-inventoried 2026-08-15 (c2-genericchat-adjudication) because the line that used to open this comment named only two callers and BOTH lost their UI in Wave 3's w7, which reads like a dead rung and is not one. THREE paths reach AiTaskType.GenericChat: (1) UnifiedAnalysisService.ExplainSuggestionAsync, the suggestion Why? button (POST /api/books/{bookId}/chapters/{chapterId}/suggestions/{suggestionId}/explain), which builds its AiRequest with TaskType=GenericChat directly, still has a live client caller, was never named here, and is the reason this rung is KEPT; (2) AnalysisType.Custom and (3) AnalysisType.QA (POST /api/books/{bookId}/ask), both mapped by AnalysisTaskMapping and both still served by the API, but API-REACHABLE ONLY since w7 removed the free-form Custom pass and the dashboard ask card from the client without touching either route. AiTaskType.Translation shares this rung's prompt arm but has no live producer (AiAnalysisService is registered in DI and injected nowhere; UnifiedAnalysisService superseded it). All three surfaces are pinned by Pagedraft.Api.Tests/GenericChatCallerSetTests. Free-form Custom prompts and QA send the WHOLE chapter as input. WITHOUT this entry GenericChat falls back to the base Ollama window (NumCtx=8192); a large chapter (e.g. 23k chars ≈ 15k+ Hebrew tokens) overflows it, Ollama TRUNCATES the prompt, and because the instruction/question sits at the START of the prompt it gets dropped — the model then sees only chapter text with no task and returns a 1-token fragment (observed live: 'סי'). NumCtx=16384 matches LinguisticAnalysis/Summarization and fits a full chapter + the question; NumPredict=2048 is ample for a free-form answer (think=false keeps output short). DO NOT WIDEN NumCtx without a measurement plan: chatbot phase B's standing caveat binds this rung too, and this is a chat-shaped window on the same 8GB GPU host, so a bigger window is a KV-cache cost paid on every call, not a free improvement.
ProviderSettings._comment_Ollama_ProductChat: Grounded product Q&A over the shipped guides corpus (chatbot phase A, d1 item 4 / c1). NumCtx=16384 is LOAD-BEARING, not a copy of the neighbours: d1's retrieval token math is computed against exactly this window. The endpoint stuffs the top N=4 WHOLE guide files into every prompt, and the Hebrew worst case (90-faq.he.md + 30-chapter-editing-passes.he.md + 00-workflow-overview.he.md + 20-book-setup-and-intelligence.he.md = 17,401 chars at ~2 chars/token on a Latin-centric BPE vocabulary) is ~8,700 tokens, leaving ~5,600 for the grounding system prompt and the capped conversation history once NumPredict 2048 is reserved. Shipping a SMALLER NumCtx does not degrade gracefully: Ollama truncates the prompt from the START, which is where the guides sit, so the model would answer from its own knowledge of the product while the response still claimed to be grounded and still carried guide-id citations. That is the precise failure this whole phase exists to prevent. NumPredict=2048 is ample for a chat answer (think=false keeps output short). Temperature 0.1 rather than the 0.2 every other entry uses is the ONE feature-specific deviation, and it is deliberate: grounded factual answers benefit from lower sampling variance, and the plan's central risk (confident invention) is a HALT-grade concern rather than a quality score. KEEP IN SYNC with FeatureModels:ProductChat below and with the cloud counterpart OpenRouter_ProductChat (CloudTuningCoverageConfigParityTests fails the moment an Ollama_* entry loses its cloud twin).
ProviderSettings._comment_OpenRouterPerTask: CLOUD PER-TASK TUNING (model-tier-fast-thinking plan, p1-3). READ BEFORE EDITING A CLOUD ENTRY. Until p1-3 the only cloud tuning key was the flat 'OpenRouter' entry above, which sets no NumCtx. That is NOT the same as 'no opinion': ProviderTuningOptions.NumCtx defaults to 4096 and 4096 is > 0, so the flat entry WON the lookup and supplied 4096 instead of falling through. Routing BookReview at OpenRouter therefore collapsed the whole-book context budget 16384 -> 4096 and reproduced exactly the failure _comment_Ollama_BookReview above documents: input overflows the window, the prompt is truncated, the model returns a lone '{', ExtractJson fails, EVERY dimension returns null, and the job reports Succeeded with 0 findings. Nothing logged a warning. The entries below close that hole; CloudTuningCoverageConfigParityTests fails if a task that has an Ollama_* entry loses its cloud counterpart, and BookContextAssembler.ResolveBudgetTokens now logs a de-duplicated WARNING at runtime if a whole-book task ever resolves a window at or below the class default (the guard test cannot see an appsettings.Production/env override, the log can). WHAT EACH FIELD MEANS ON A CLOUD ENTRY, which is NOT what it means on an Ollama entry: (1) MaxTokens is the ONLY tuning field that reaches the wire (OpenAiProvider.BuildPayload sends model/messages/temperature/max_tokens and nothing else), and on a PAID provider an oversized cap is direct cost exposure, so each value below is the measured output size of that task's OWN prompt rather than the flat entry's one-size 5120. That deliberately LOWERS the cap for Summarization/GenericChat/AnalysisRepair (2048) and TermRepair (256), whose prompts ask for a small answer. (2) NumCtx is NEVER sent to a cloud provider. It is a LOCAL DECLARATION of the routed model's usable window that BookContextAssembler.ResolveBudgetTokens and UnifiedAnalysisService.EffectiveChunkTargetWords size input against. Declaring it too LARGE re-creates the truncation above at a higher threshold with nothing to catch it; too SMALL drops chapters. (3) RepeatPenalty is deliberately ABSENT: the OpenAI-compatible payload has no such field, so Ollama_LineEdit's RepeatPenalty 1.3 (the Dicta repetition-loop fix) has NO cloud counterpart and writing one here would be dead config. WHY THE WINDOWS MIRROR THE OLLAMA VALUES RATHER THAN THE MODEL'S REAL MAXIMUM: the wired cloud candidate google/gemma-4-31b-it advertises context_length 262144 and max_completion_tokens 262144 on OpenRouter (catalog read 2026-07-28; the ':free' variant caps output at 32768), so 16384 sits 16x inside it and cannot overflow it or a smaller-window backend OpenRouter may route that model id to. Mirroring the local window ON PURPOSE means switching a task to the cloud tier changes ONE variable, the MODEL, which is exactly what phase 2 has to measure; a larger cloud budget would confound that comparison and no measurement yet says more context helps. Raising a window is a deliberate one-line change per task AFTER p2 measures it, not a default. For scale: gemma-4-31b-it is $0.14/1M input tokens, so a 16384-token book budget is ~$0.0023 of input per review window call, while declaring the full 262144 would make it ~$0.018 per call on every window of every review for an unmeasured benefit. Proofread/LineEdit carry an EXPLICIT 4096 because their Ollama counterparts omit NumCtx and therefore resolve 4096; writing it out keeps the cloud entries free of the very silent-default trap this block documents. PRIVACY: every entry here means an unpublished manuscript leaves the machine. These keys only TUNE; they do not route. Nothing reaches OpenRouter until an Ai:FeatureModels entry names Provider=OpenRouter.
ProviderSettings._comment_OpenRouter_ProductChat: Cloud counterpart of Ollama_ProductChat (chatbot phase A, c1), written per _comment_OpenRouterPerTask's field semantics, which are NOT the Ollama entry's. MaxTokens 2048 is the only field that reaches the wire and is sized to this task's REAL answer size (a chat reply), not to the flat entry's one-size 5120 - on a paid provider an oversized output cap is direct cost exposure. NumCtx 16384 is a LOCAL declaration only (no cloud payload carries it) and mirrors the Ollama window ON PURPOSE, because d1's whole-file retrieval math is against 16384 and because switching a task to the cloud tier must change exactly ONE variable, the MODEL. No NumPredict and no RepeatPenalty: neither exists in the OpenAI-compatible payload, so writing either would be dead config that reads as though it were tuned (EveryCloudEntry_SetsMaxTokens_AndLeavesNumPredictAtTheClassDefault pins that). Temperature 0.1 carries the local entry's one deliberate deviation forward for the same reason it exists there: grounded factual answers want low sampling variance. THIS KEY ONLY TUNES; it does not route. Nothing reaches OpenRouter until an Ai:FeatureModels entry names Provider=OpenRouter, and ProductChat is deliberately NOT tierable (it is app-level, not book-scoped, so there is no book id to resolve a tier from).
ProviderSettings._comment_CloudBookReviewFloor: BOOKREVIEW WINDOW FLOOR ON EVERY PROVIDER (p1-3). OpenAI / Azure / Anthropic are NOT wired tier targets (the model-tier plan defers them explicitly) and deliberately have no full per-task mirror, so CloudTuningCoverageConfigParityTests waives them BY NAME from the mirror guard. BookReview is the one exception and it is NOT waivable: it is the task whose under-sizing failure is TOTAL and SILENT (every dimension null, job still reports Succeeded), so it gets an explicit window on EVERY provider in AiProviderRegistry and BookReviewWindow_IsNeverTheClassDefault_UnderAnyRegisteredProvider asserts it. NumCtx 16384 sits well inside each family's real window (gpt-4o 128k, claude-3-5-sonnet 200k) and MaxTokens 6144 inside each family's output cap (claude-3-5-sonnet allows 8192), so these are safe wherever they land. Registering a new provider in AiProviderRegistry without adding its BookReview entry here turns that test red, which is the point: this bug must not be able to return silently.

FeatureModels._comment_ProofreadModel: KEEP IN SYNC: Proofread:Model is duplicated in ProofreadQualityTests.ProofreadModel (Pagedraft.Api.Tests/LanguageEngine/ProofreadQualityTests.cs). Update both when changing the model. NO LONGER HAND-POLICED (2026-07-29, fixes-plan be-c05, restated here by final-r02 because this is the comment an appsettings editor reads): HarnessConfigParityTests.TheProofreadHarnessModelConstant_EqualsTheShippedProofreadFeatureModel binds THIS file and goes red if a model swap touches only one side, and the sibling facts in that class also pin Ollama_Proofread / OpenRouter_Proofread against what the harness installs. The two are still separate literals - the bake-off wires its own in-memory config on purpose so a sweep can drive any model - so you must still edit both; the pin is what tells you when you forgot. RESOLVED 2026-07-29 (model-tier-fast-thinking plan, p2-3) - THIS QUESTION IS NO LONGER OPEN. The 2026-07-27 verdict was KEEP DictaLM-3.0 pending an n>=3 re-run, because two runs disagreed: run 1 read 'gemma4 beats Dicta by 35%' and run 2 read a dead tie with Dicta 20 points better on recall. That re-run is done at n=5 per candidate, all 93 gold cases, 0 errors, nothing capped, production-faithful tuning (Ollama_Proofread NumPredict 4096). RESULT (min/median/max): gemma4:12b F0.5 0.332/0.353/0.387, precision 30/32/35%, recall 65/65/65%, fp-rate 15/18/22%. DictaLM-3.0 F0.5 0.261/0.287/0.337, precision 23/25/29%, recall 70/70/85%, fp-rate 31/32/33%. Overreach 0/4 for BOTH in all 10 runs, so the hard precision gate is unchanged. Precision and false-positive rate are FULLY DISJOINT in gemma4:12b's favour (25/25 and 0/25 pairwise); recall is FULLY DISJOINT in Dicta's favour. F0.5 - the pre-registered precision-weighted ranking metric - favours gemma4:12b 24/25 pairwise. STABILITY, a selection criterion in its own right, also favours gemma4:12b: its recall is dead flat (spread 0 across 5 runs) against Dicta's 15-point swing. Dicta's only win is recall, bought by correcting far more aggressively - it puts a spurious correction on ~1 in 3 clean sentences (fp-rate 31-33%) against gemma4:12b's 15-22%. VERDICT: SWITCHED to gemma4:12b for Hebrew Proofread. HONEST LIMITS: (a) the F0.5 median gap (0.066) is SMALLER than Dicta's own within-model spread (0.076), so F0.5 alone would not settle it - what settles it is fp-rate, the only metric whose worst-case margin (9 pts) exceeds BOTH within-model spreads, plus fully-disjoint precision; (b) model-only recall genuinely regresses 70-85% -> 65%, though production merges a deterministic KtivMaleChecker (UnifiedAnalysisService.cs:3565) that this gold harness does NOT run, so part of Hebrew spelling recall is supplied model-independently - inferred, NOT measured; (c) the gold harness drives IAiRouter single-shot and BYPASSES chunking, so this does not automatically transfer to the real chunked path for a long chapter. SCOPE: Proofread only. LineEdit still routes to DictaLM-3.0 and is NOT measured by this gold (it has its own decoding quirk - see Ollama_LineEdit RepeatPenalty 1.3); it needs its own bake-off. METHODOLOGY RULE THAT STILL STANDS: a SINGLE bake-off run cannot decide a model swap - every other model figure in these comments is a single-run point estimate, so run n>=5 and compare distributions AND spread before changing any wired model. TIER DECISION (p2-4, 2026-07-29, layered on top of the MODEL decision above, not replacing it): the model-tier-fast-thinking plan's phase 2 asked a SEPARATE question - not which local model to ship, but whether a cloud tier measurably beats whichever local model ships - and the verdict for Hebrew Proofread is GO. Judged against THIS key's current value (gemma4:12b, not the outgoing DictaLM-3.0), cloud (OpenRouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it, n=3) scores F0.5 0.521/0.602/0.625, precision 48/59/61%, recall 65/70/75%, fp-rate 7/7/8%, overreach 0/4, against local's F0.5 0.332/0.353/0.387, precision 30/32/35%, recall 65/65/65%, fp-rate 15/18/22%. F0.5, precision and false-positive-rate all clear the bar (margin exceeds the larger within-model spread on each); recall is no longer a cloud loss now that the local incumbent is gemma4:12b rather than Dicta (cloud's 65-75% sits at-or-above local's flat 65%). Caveats carried forward unchanged from both decisions: single-shot harness that bypasses chunking and the deterministic KtivMaleChecker merge, so this does not automatically validate the real chunked production path; cloud was measured at the harness's un-wired MaxTokens 2048 and local at production-faithful NumPredict 4096, judged inert for cloud too because realized cloud output was 24-61 tokens/case (well under either cap). SCOPE: Hebrew Proofread only - Proofread_en has never been measured against cloud and this GO must not be extended to it. Full margins, residual risk and phase-3 scope: see '## p2 decision' in src/.cursor/plans/_todo/model-tier-fast-thinking-2026-07-28.plan.md. THE THINKING TIER THIS GO FUNDS IS NOW SHIPPED (p3-2..p3-4): a book opts in via PUT /api/books/{bookId}/ai-tier, and an opted-in book's Hebrew Proofread routes through the separate 'Proofread_thinking' key below (see _comment_ModelTier) - Hebrew only, because 'Proofread_en' outranks the tier rung by design, so English proofreading stays local on both tiers. This bare key's value (gemma4:12b) stays the FAST-tier default for every book. Do NOT flip Provider=OpenRouter on THIS bare key - that would move every book's Hebrew proofread to cloud with no per-book consent.

FeatureModels._comment_BookReview: Whole-book developmental review (wb2). CLOUD MAX-QUALITY = OpenRouter / google/gemma-4-31b-it - the ~31B model that does NOT fit the 8 GB dev GPU; it is the structured-review quality ceiling for FUTURE GPU-server hosting, not the local default. Active value is Ollama/gemma4:12b - the strongest LOCAL structured model per the bake-off (same model LinguisticAnalysis uses) for free/offline/private use. TIER DECISION (p2-4, model-tier-fast-thinking plan, 2026-07-29): NO-GO for a cloud tier on THIS task, because it is UNMEASURED, not because it lost. BookReviewQualityTests.CreateRouter hard-codes provider=Ollama and never registers OpenRouter, so no cloud-routed BookReview has ever been run (p1-3's RULE 0 hand-off is still OPEN). FeatureModels._comment_ModelTier: THE THINKING-TIER KEYS (model-tier-fast-thinking plan, p3-2). READ BEFORE ADDING ONE. A key of the form '{Task}_thinking' is consulted ONLY when a book has opted in (Book.AiTier = 'thinking'); the bare '{Task}' key above is the FAST tier and stays the default for every book. There are exactly TWO such keys and there may not be a third without a measurement, because p2-4's GO is PER TASK: GO for LinguisticAnalysis (cloud composite 0.857-0.900 vs local 0.689-0.732, n=3 each, disjoint ranges, margin ~2.9x the within-model spread) and GO for HEBREW Proofread (F0.5 0.521-0.625 vs 0.332-0.387; precision 48-61% vs 30-35%; false-positive rate 7-8% vs 15-22%; all three disjoint against the CURRENT gemma4:12b incumbent). NO-GO, unmeasured, for BookReview (the bake-off harness cannot even route OpenRouter) and for Proofread_en (never measured against cloud). LineEdit / Summarization / AnalysisRepair / GenericChat are unmeasured; TermRepair is additionally routing-only by a standing cost/privacy decision independent of quality (see _comment_TermRepair). FOUR THINGS ENFORCE THAT, so adding a key here is not sufficient to widen the tier and is not silently tolerated either: (E1) a book stores ONE tier token, never a task->model map, so no book can hold a value meaning 'BookReview at OpenRouter'; (E2) AiTierPolicy.TieredTasks is the ONE allowlist, read by both LinguisticModelResolver.ResolveForTask and AiRouter.ResolveSelection - a '{Task}_thinking' key for a task outside it is never looked up; (E3) PRECEDENCE is {task}_{lang} -> {task}_{tier} -> {task} -> DefaultProvider/DefaultModel, so 'Proofread_en' OUTRANKS 'Proofread_thinking' and an English book on the thinking tier resolves the local English model and cannot reach the tier rung - which is how 'Hebrew Proofread only' is expressed, since Proofread_en is a key suffix and not an AiTaskType; there is deliberately NO '{task}_{lang}_{tier}' rung and writing 'Proofread_en_thinking' fails the guard; (E4) AiTierConfigParityTests binds THIS file and fails on a '{Task}_thinking' key outside the allowlist, on any 'Proofread_en_thinking' form, on a dead '{Task}_fast' key, and on TermRepair entering the allowlist. PRIVACY: both keys below route to a third-party provider, so choosing the thinking tier means an unpublished manuscript leaves the machine. It is opt-in per book and null/absent/unrecognised parses to fast. KILL-SWITCH: delete these two keys (or clear their Provider/Model - the shared both-non-empty predicate makes a half-configured entry fall through), and every book resolves the local models again with no code change. KEEP IN SYNC with Ai:ProviderSettings:OpenRouter_Proofread / OpenRouter_LinguisticAnalysis above, which size these routes' windows and output caps.

Ai._comment_BookReviewSingleCombined: Whole-book review fan-out strategy (wb2-r02). TRUE (default) runs ONE combined LLM call assessing all six dimensions (plot/character/pacing/tone/theme/continuity) over a single assembled book context; FALSE falls back to the per-dimension fan-out (six calls capped by MaxParallelBookReviewDimensions). Default is single-combined because wb2-c04 measured per-dimension (6 calls/book) as a QUALITY TIE with single-combined (1 call/book) - same planted-recall, same 0 clean false positives, identical composite - at 6x the model calls and more noise; wb2-c06 then showed the per-dimension parallel fan-out CRASHES the 8 GB dev GPU on big books while a single combined call completes. Per-dimension is kept reversible behind this toggle ONLY for a future larger-GPU re-measure; set false to use it.
Ai._comment_Tier: MODEL-TIER SURFACE POLICY (tier-ux-rework plan, c2). This block does NOT route anything - routing is Ai:FeatureModels plus AiTierPolicy.TieredTasks - it says how the tier CONTROL must behave on this deployment. ConsentRequired=true means the client renders an explicit confirm step before a task is committed to the thinking tier. It is TRUE here because in dev the fast tier is local Ollama and the thinking tier is a third-party cloud provider, so 'this sends your unpublished manuscript off this machine' is a true and new statement at the moment of the flip. appsettings.Production.json sets it FALSE, explicitly rather than by inheritance (Production REPLACES an object block rather than merging into it, so an omitted key there would fall back to the class default, not to this value): in a hosted deployment BOTH tiers already run off-machine, so the step would ask for consent to something that already happened on the fast tier, which is exactly the noise that trains users to click through consent dialogs. IT IS NOT AN AUTHORIZATION GATE. The server's 409 on a 'thinking' request the deployment cannot route (AiTierStatusService/AiTierReadiness) is unconditional and completely independent of this flag; setting it false removes a UI step and removes nothing from the server. KEEP IN SYNC with appsettings.Production.json - AiTierConsentFlagConfigParityTests binds both files and pins true/false respectively, so a flip in one file alone turns red.
Ai._comment_BookReview: b8 kill-switch (Ai:BookReview:SynthesisMergeMap; full contract on BookReviewOptions.SynthesisMergeMap's xmldoc, Services/Ai/AiOptions.cs). Gates the ONLY mutation the synthesis merge-map pass can make: applying a model-proposed 'merge these near-duplicate findings' map, which DELETES the absorbed findings. SHIPS FALSE. Read this before assuming OFF means unchanged: with the switch false the merge map is still parsed, validated against the digest, resolved and LOGGED (measure mode) - the PROMPT is not gated by this switch (gating it would leave nothing to measure), so the model still sees the merge contract and answers a DIFFERENT prompt than pre-b8; OFF is a third behaviour, not a byte-identical revert. Ships OFF because the live gate MEASURED harm: gemma4:12b falsely merged two unrelated findings that only shared a mentioned name, and those were a dimension's ONLY two findings, so the dimension vanished from the score panel. Flip only against a model whose measure-mode log has been read and is clean, mirroring the dynamic-term-repair rollout. KEEP IN SYNC with appsettings.Production.json; SynthesisMergeMapConfigParityTests binds both files and pins this value to false - a future flip must turn that test red.
Ai._comment_OllamaParallel: For parallel chunk processing, set env OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2 (or higher) where Ollama runs; restart Ollama after changing.
Ai._comment_HebrewStyle: Deterministic Hebrew-orthography switches for the copyedit layer. TWO KINDS, and they are not interchangeable. (1) EnforceKtivMale=true (default) is HOUSE STYLE: it appends deterministic haser->male full-spelling suggestions to Hebrew proofread results; set false for houses that do not normalize to ktiv-male. (2) DropOrthographicallyImpossibleSuggestions=true (default) is a CORRECTNESS SAFETY NET, not a taste preference: it withholds a proofread suggestion whose replacement introduces a mechanically impossible Hebrew word - a final form (kaf/mem/nun/pe/tsadi sofit) in a NON-FINAL position - into an original span that was itself clean. READ ITS SCOPE HONESTLY: on the corpus that motivated it (the 2026-08-05 real-prose measurement, 128 suggestions over twelve twice-proofread manuscript passages) the rule fires on exactly ONE suggestion, and that one belongs to the ARM A column, not the shipped default's; it reaches ZERO of the ten Hebrew non-words the shipped prompt produced. It is a net for one impossible shape, NOT a remedy for model-authored non-words. It defaults ON because the shape it rejects is wrong in every register and house style, because it makes no model call, and because its drop is bounded so it cannot suppress a legal correction (it only ever removes a replacement that INTRODUCES the impossible word). That is a different posture from Ai:ProofreadPrompt:OverlapReferentLicence, which defaults OFF because it CHANGES THE PROMPT; this switch changes no prompt and no model input. Every drop is logged at Warning with the offending word and counted on AnalysisRunLogs.SuppressedSuggestionCount (beside SuggestionCount), so a run that dropped three is distinguishable from a run that dropped none. Kill switch: set false to restore the pre-guard suggestion list byte for byte. NOTE appsettings.Production.json declares no Ai:HebrewStyle block, so THESE values survive the Production layer unchanged and are what a hosted deployment runs; the class defaults in HebrewStyleOptions govern only programmatic/test construction and are kept identical to these. HebrewStyleConfigParityTests pins both halves. See HebrewOrthographyShapeGuard and RealProseNonWordResidue.
Ai._comment_ProofreadPrompt: Per-chunk proofread PROMPT ARMS (PromptFactory.BuildProofreadChunkPrompt only - the single-shot path composes through GetAnalysisPrompt and is not touched). EVERY switch here defaults FALSE and the shipped value below is FALSE, so the composed per-chunk prompt is byte-identical to the pre-arm one; ProofreadPromptArmTests pins that identity. OverlapReferentLicence re-lands ARM A of referent-carry-forward-2026-08-04 VERBATIM: it appends an explicit pronoun-resolution licence to the [CONTEXT_BEFORE] instruction line. That arm was REJECTED on chunked agreement recall (0/15 on its own acceptance fixture), and its precision side effect (a synthetic ~38% over-correction cut) was then measured on real twice-proofread prose on 2026-08-05 and DID NOT REPRODUCE: better on only 5 of 12 passages, one-sided p=0.363, verdict DO NOT SHIP - see RealProseArmMeasurement and ProofreadStandingFloor.RetiredInterventions (id referent-carry-forward.ARM_A.OverlapLicence). The lead is CLOSED and has now been opened twice - DO NOT re-open it. The switch is kept ONLY so any future measurement costs a session rather than a re-implementation; turning it on requires a NEW plan with a new pre-stated decision rule.
Ai._comment_AnalysisRepair: Analysis-output repair layer (analysis-output-repair plan, p6-config; Mode added by dynamic-term-repair-design plan, d4). Governs the repair stages in UnifiedAnalysisService.ApplyAnalysisRepairAsync AND the whole-book review ENGINE-path hook in BookReviewService (f5-wire glossary + d4-wire dynamic). FOUR states, layered: (1) Enabled=false -> FULL no-op (no stage runs). (2) Enabled=true + GuardOnly=true -> the Mode-selected stage(s) ONLY, no value-scoped LLM (the SHIPPED DEFAULT below, per the p3-gate GUARD-ONLY decision: the glossary is deterministic+fail-safe+validated, while the value-scoped LLM showed an over-rewrite tendency on mixed leak+prose fields, so it stays opt-in). (3) Enabled=true + GuardOnly=false -> Mode-selected stage(s) + value-scoped LLM repair (guard-gated+fail-safe inside the service; a clean field makes ZERO model calls). (4) Mode (Off/Glossary/Dynamic/GlossaryThenDynamic; SHIPPED DEFAULT = GlossaryThenDynamic, i.e. glossary fast-path THEN the dynamic span-scoped pass, with Mode=Glossary/Off the rollback/kill-switch that reproduces the pre-d4 glossary-only behaviour) selects WHICH of the deterministic glossary vs the dynamic span-scoped pass (DynamicTermRepairService) run — see AnalysisRepairMode in Services/Ai/AiOptions.cs. This ON default was RE-AUTHORISED on 2026-07-12 (be-c08) after a re-measure through the REAL BookEntityProvider path on the LOCAL tier: out-of-glossary cleaning 100% (10/10, unchanged by an adversarial per-book entity set), legitimate-term preservation 100% (21/21), false positives 0, over-rewrite 0, and 0 legitimate values reaching the model (see docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md section 18). NOTE the CLASS default in AiOptions.AnalysisRepairOptions deliberately stays Glossary: that is the safe posture for programmatic/test construction, not a contradiction of this shipped value, and AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests binds THIS file to prove which stages actually ship. PerType gates repair per AnalysisType name (Summarization/LiteraryAnalysis/LinguisticAnalysis/LineEdit, plus the f5-wire book-level structured-Hebrew-prose types BookOverview/CharacterAnalysis/StoryAnalysis/QA, the whole-book BookReview engine hook, and - since f2 on 2026-07-28 - Synopsis, the SECOND plain-text type alongside Summarization; a type absent/false is skipped; Proofread is NEVER repaired regardless). BookReview never runs the value-scoped LLM stage regardless of GuardOnly (glossary/dynamic only). KEEP IN SYNC with AiOptions.AnalysisRepairOptions; Model MUST match Ai:FeatureModels:AnalysisRepair (and Ai:ProviderSettings:Ollama_AnalysisRepair) - those keys do the routing, this Model documents the intended repair model. PERTYPE KEEP-IN-SYNC (h3, analysis-repair-pertype-coverage-holes plan, 2026-07-28): this PerType map MUST mirror appsettings.Production.json's Ai:AnalysisRepair:PerType byte-for-byte - Production fully OVERRIDES this block rather than merging with it, so a key added to one file and not the other silently drifts the gate between environments; guarded by AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.PerType_BaseAndProduction_AreEqual and the enum-completeness oracle EveryAnalysisType_HasAnExplicitRepairCoverageDecision (the latter forces a Repaired-or-DeliberatelyExcluded decision for EVERY AnalysisType, not just parity between the two files, so a newly added enum member cannot slip through undecided). A PerType key present-and-true with NO dispatch arm in the per-type dispatch switches is DEAD CONFIG that claims coverage it cannot deliver. THERE ARE THREE such switches, not two (be-c01, 2026-07-28): GlossaryRepairPass.Apply and DynamicTermRepairService.ApplyAsync (both deterministic, both run under the shipped GuardOnly=true) plus AnalysisRepairService.RepairAnalysisAsync (the value-scoped LLM stage, reached only in state (3) above). A type wired into some and not others ships a FRACTION of the layer, which is acceptable only as a recorded decision - Synopsis is the one such case: it is wired into the two DETERMINISTIC switches only and is deliberately NOT an arm in AnalysisRepairService.RepairAnalysisAsync, so GuardOnly=false adds nothing for it - the argument and its reversal condition live at that switch's default: arm (see _comment_PerTypeExclusions below and docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md section 4.1) - "BookOverview": true already ships as a live example: it IS a dispatch target in all three switches, but on its only real producer path (BuildBookProfileAsync's RunRawAsync(structuredJson: null) call) both switches blank-guard to a no-op, and BookOverview's one repairable field (Summary) is discarded before persistence anyway, so the key is a no-op there by construction (see docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md section 4.1 and the plan's '## Investigation findings'). Enabling a type whose routed AiTaskType model differs from Ai:FeatureModels:TermRepair (currently gemma4:12b) ADDS cross-model GPU-swap surface on a single-GPU host (OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1) per leaking value - this is exactly why Synopsis (-> Summarization -> qwen3.5:9b) and Custom (-> GenericChat -> qwen3.5:9b) were investigated rather than casually enabled. As of 2026-07-28 (f2) Synopsis is ENABLED - q2 cleared the precision bar it failed under q1 (100% (6/6) preservation, 0 false positives, over-rewrite 0) and the swap cost was accepted explicitly rather than overlooked - while Custom stays DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. See PerType's own _comment_PerTypeExclusions below, plus docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md sections 4.1 / 4.2 / 19.4 and the plans' '## d1 decision', '## c1 findings', '## q2 quality-gate results' and '## f2 outcome'.
Ai._comment_SummaryBatchWindowChapters: be-c03 CHECKPOINT WINDOW for BookIntelligenceService.SummarizeChaptersCoreAsync. The chapter-summary pass groups chapters into windows of this size and runs summarize -> ONE repair pass -> persist per window, so the TermRepair model loads at most once per WINDOW rather than once per leaking chapter (that is the s2 batching win) while each completed window is durably committed. It is a LIVENESS bound, not a quality knob: before it existed the pass had a single commit at the very end, so a client reload, a gateway idle ceiling, or the OOM-wedged Ollama runner this host has actually produced (HTTP 500 after ~30 minutes, memory pagedraft-ollama-8gb-tuning) discarded EVERY chapter - and since such a failure recurs at roughly the same point, the retry never converged. Sized from the MEASURED cost in docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md section 19: ~18-27 s per chapter, so 10 chapters bounds the work at risk to ~3-4.5 minutes; this project's own corpus has an 80-chapter book whose first pass is 24-37 minutes. Lowering it does NOT cost a swap per window on a healthy corpus: a window whose chapters all come back CLEAN makes no repair model call at all (section 19.1) and the measured leak rate is ~3% (section 19.4), so the expected swap count is min(windows, leaking chapters) either way. Raising it to at or above a book's chapter count reproduces the original single-commit behaviour exactly; a non-positive value is CLAMPED to the default (10) rather than meaning 'no windowing'. KEEP IN SYNC with appsettings.Production.json - AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.SummaryBatchWindowChapters_BaseAndProduction_AreEqual fails if the two files diverge.

AnalysisRepair._comment_PerTypeExclusions: h3 (analysis-repair-pertype-coverage-holes plan, 2026-07-28) makes the per-type decisions EXPLICIT rather than merely absent, so each one is visible at the config surface instead of inferred from a missing line. An explicit false is semantically IDENTICAL to absence under AnalysisRepairGate.Evaluate (present-and-false and absent both return PerTypeExcluded). Custom: DELIBERATELY false (d1, reasoning NARROWED by c1) - its instruction is user-authored (req.CustomPrompt), so the output is legitimately English / bilingual / quoted / tabular, which falsifies the layer's foreign-script=leak premise; and repair cost is one model call per foreign WORD with no cap, so an English answer would be both mistranslated and a several-hundred-call GPU wedge. c1 then MEASURED the real corpus (analysis-repair-coverage-followups plan, 2026-07-28): n=16 rows / 6 distinct instructions / 1 user / 2 books, Hebrew script fraction 1.0000 on EVERY row, max offline REPAIR-classified run count 0, rows with at least one repair run 0/16 (Wilson 95% CI 0.0-19.4%) - so an enabled Custom repair would clean NOTHING on the real data while the uncapped cost stays merely unsampled, and the pick-frequency assumption remains un-measured. Note the exclusion does not rest on this key alone: Custom has NO dispatch arm in ANY of the THREE per-type dispatch switches (GlossaryRepairPass.Apply, DynamicTermRepairService.ApplyAsync, AnalysisRepairService.RepairAnalysisAsync), so flipping this key to true today would change nothing at all - enabling it means adding three dispatch arms first. See the plan's '## d1 decision' and '## c1 findings'. Synopsis: WAS deliberately false (q1: 83% preservation, 1 false positive) and is now TRUE (f2, 2026-07-28). q2 RE-MEASURED it on q1's OWN fixtures after ForeignRunClassifier rule (7b) landed, and the section-18.2 bar CLEARED: preservation 100% (6/6), false positives 0, over-rewrite 0, cleaning 100% (3/3), on the shipped LOCAL tier (Ollama | gemma4:12b) and reproduced identically on cloud gemma-4-31b-it. READ THAT 100% CORRECTLY: 0 of the 6 legitimate values reach the model, so it is a property of the DETERMINISTIC GATE (1 entity-gated, 5 classifier-rule-gated, 0 model) and not of gemma4:12b - rule (7b) does not make the model better at proper nouns, it stops asking it. THE GPU-SWAP COST IS ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY, not overlooked: Synopsis routes to AiTaskType.Summarization -> qwen3.5:9b while Ai:FeatureModels:TermRepair is gemma4:12b, so on an OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1 host every LEAKING synopsis costs a cross-model load (~21.5-34.3s, asymmetric, docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md section 19.2) plus a load back on the next Summarization-family call. It is bounded to GENUINE leaks - a clean synopsis makes ZERO model calls and q2 measured 0/6 legitimate values reaching the model - and Synopsis is produced ONCE per profile build, not once per chapter, on a path (BuildBookProfileAsync) that already interleaves qwen3.5:9b and gemma4:12b generation with zero repair involvement. That is the same trade s4 already ACCEPTED (docs section 19.4). RESIDUAL RISK, stated so it is not forgotten: rule (7b) spares a LINE-HEAD proper noun only (be-c03 restated it as a LINE head - ONE hard line break is enough, a blank line is NOT required, which is what the real persisted Synopsis / SummaryText prose actually uses); an external proper noun at a MID-LINE sentence head still reaches the repair model, and a synopsis is the value shape most likely to name one. VALUE-SCOPED LLM CARVE-OUT (be-c01, 2026-07-28): this key wires Synopsis into the two DETERMINISTIC dispatch switches only. It is DELIBERATELY not an arm in the third, AnalysisRepairService.RepairAnalysisAsync, so setting GuardOnly=false adds nothing for Synopsis - that stage never consults ForeignRunClassifier, so rule (7b) cannot protect it, and the only measurement of a repair model rewriting Synopsis prose is q1's 83%/1-FP HALT. The argument and its reversal condition are stated at that switch's default arm; see docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md sections 4.1 / 4.2. KILL-SWITCH: set this key back to false in BOTH files (the dispatch arms may stay - the gate closes ahead of them). See the plan's '## q2 quality-gate results' and '## f2 outcome', and docs sections 4.1 / 4.2. Proofread stays ABSENT rather than explicit-false: its exclusion is architectural (output quotes verbatim manuscript spans; repairing them would corrupt the suggestion diff), already stated independently in docs section 4 and inside all three dispatch switches' own default/fallback arms, and PerType is a map of things that MAY be flipped on - an explicit false here could misleadingly suggest Proofread is a config-level toggle, when enabling it would require rewriting the dispatch switches and would violate the verbatim-manuscript-span design rule. AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.EveryAnalysisType_HasAnExplicitRepairCoverageDecision (h2) accepts absent OR present-and-false for an excluded type, so this asymmetry between Custom and Proofread is a deliberate choice, not an inconsistency. KEEP THIS IN SYNC with the sibling appsettings file's own _comment_PerTypeExclusions (byte-identical) - AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.PerType_BaseAndProduction_AreEqual only compares the boolean PerType values, not this comment, but drift here would make the two files' documented rationale disagree.
